title: Gautam Gambhir, Aaqib Javed part of same management team:  Iceland Cricket creates hilarious 'international management personnel of nightmares'
description: With the recent management decisions making a mockery of Pakistani cricket, Iceland Cricket has now dragged Gautam Gambhir into the fray.
fullText:
Iceland Cricket published a viral "management personnel of nightmares" poking fun at recent off-field controversies across world cricket.

The mock team features India's Gautam Gambhir as head coach, Pakistan's Aaqib Javed as head of selectors, and Imam-ul-Haq as team physio.

Rob Key and Harry Brook were targeted over England's relaxed, golf-heavy team culture and off-field banter.

Iceland Cricket's social media account, long the sport's most reliable satirical mirror, has delivered another sharp critique of international cricket's current administrative absurdities.

In a post that quickly went viral across the cricket community, the handle assembled a mock "international management personnel of nightmares."

The satirical list takes aim at the ongoing chaos spanning several major boards. From Gautam Gambhir's intense coaching persona in India and Aaqib Javed's volatile selection policies in Pakistan to England's leisure-heavy "Bazball" team culture, it takes a dig at everyone.

The mock setup weaves together current figures whose recent public controversies, tactical friction, or off-field reputations make them a uniquely disastrous combination on paper.

MORE: Former Pakistan selector claims Babar Azam 'protected' Imam-ul-Haq in faking injury

At the top of this fictional chain of command sits Gautam Gambhir as head coach, operating alongside Aaqib Javed as head of selectors. The joke lands because of the sheer operational paradox it presents. Combining Gambhir's uncompromising, high-pressure persona with Aaqib's recent habit of purging senior players mid-series is a recipe for instant combustion.

We can create a current international management personnel of nightmares:

Head coach: Gautam Gambhir
Head of selectors: Aqib Javed
Captain and post-match party organiser: Harry Brook
Director of golf: Rob Key
Physio: Imam-ul-Haq

In reality, marrying Gambhir's demand for militant discipline with Aaqib's erratic selection resets would guarantee a total dressing-room mutiny before the tea break on day one. The lower half of the management structure is equally pointed.

Assigning Imam-ul-Haq the role of "Team Physio" is a direct, brutal nod to the ongoing fallout from the Lord's Test. With the opener's calf strain conveniently coinciding with Pakistan's second-innings collapse, handing Imam the medical kit is satire operating at its sharpest.

Meanwhile, England's laid-back, vibecentric ethos gets its own designated department. Naming Rob Key as "Director of Golf" and Harry Brook as "Captain and post-match party organiser" perfectly mocks the leisure-heavy culture defining the Bazball era.

MORE: 'Can't say he faked it, but…': PCB director Aaqib Javed wants inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq's injury at Lord's

The humour in Iceland Cricket's tweet relies entirely on raw accuracy. Assigning Imam-ul-Haq the role of "Team Physio" is a direct nod to the recent controversy at Lord's, where the opener's calf strain coincided with a second-innings collapse and subsequent allegations from former selectors regarding manipulated fitness reports.

Similarly, pairing Gambhir's uncompromising, high-pressure coaching environment with Aaqib Javed's erratic selection policy creates an operational paradox.

In real life, combining Gambhir's demand for rigid intensity with Aaqib's habit of purging senior players mid-series would guarantee total dressing-room collapse within a week.

For England, naming Rob Key as "Director of Golf" and Harry Brook as "Post-Match Party Organiser" mocks the laid-back, vibecentric ethos that has defined the team's leadership. While effective during winning stretches, that casual posture routinely draws public cynicism the moment results slip on away tours.

There is, however, a grim reality buried in the humor. Until major boards can display a modicum of operational stability and sound decision-making, supporters will continue to find more clarity in a joke tweet from Reykjavik than in the official communications coming out of Lahore, London, or Mumbai.

fullText:
As Rockstar’s blockbuster prepares to dominate the headlines, it’s time for the mainstream media to stop treating video games as a novelty that needs explaining

Predictably, the Grand Theft Auto VI “extended look” which premiered on Netflix last week was a success for all involved. The 30-minute preview scorched to No 1 on the viewing chart and even brought the site down for a few minutes as millions of gamers tried to watch what was, effectively, a very long teaser trailer. According to data collated by Eurogamer, more than 9,000 Twitch streamers covered the show leading to 5,227,798 hours of viewing there alone. And this was just the beginning of what will surely be two months of escalating hype – and unprecedented media attention.

Call me cynical, but I suspect the coverage of GTA VI in the media over the next few weeks will follow a familiar pattern. Mostly, it will be five-minute slots wedged in near the end of news bulletins in which games journalists, industry analysts and other pundits will be asked why the game is such a big deal, how much it cost to make and how much revenue it will generate. Perhaps a few will try to reignite the hoary old “violence in video games” debate, there will be presenters laughingly admitting they’ve not touched a game since Pac-Man, rolling their eyes and wallowing in their ignorance, in a way they never would while discussing any other art form. Somebody will venture the subversive view that “games are no longer just for kids”; somebody else will say “games make more money than films and music put together”. And that will be that, job done for another decade … or until there’s a funny story about Pokémon.

I hope I’m wrong. I hope, at least, the BBC, which employs plenty of staff who understand video games, will make time in its schedule to take a good look at GTA VI – its themes and influences, its creators, its place in the wider culture of games and entertainment. Sure, arts coverage on BBC television has been in decline for years, with the broadcaster shifting this content to digital platforms, but I saw plenty of in-depth analysis of Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey, looking at the quality of its translation, its depiction of female characters, its use of practical effects. I didn’t see a single presenter shrugging, looking comedically bewildered and admitting they’d not read Homer since secondary school.

On top of this, whatever mainstream media attention GTA VI does get it will come at the expense of covering other titles. Because, when the next video game story comes up in the wake of Rockstar’s behemoth, TV and radio editors and producers will be thinking, “Oh, we covered games last month.”

The thing is, GTA is a phenomenon – it looks gorgeous, it looks vast, and it will sell many millions of copies. The series’ notoriety transcends the medium. But is it the most interesting video game since GTA V? So much has changed since then. We’ve explored the fascinating, innovative open worlds of Elden Ring, Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and No Man’s Sky (an open galaxy!); we’ve seen brutal adult themes explored in The Last of Us: Part 2 and Silent Hill; we’ve experienced dizzying narrative innovations via Disco Elysium, Split Fiction and Lost Records: Bloom & Rage. All of these deserved at least a portion of that GTA screen and radio time.

True, some games have drawn similar levels of media attention. Minecraft and Fortnite receive regular coverage, but almost always because of concerns over children and games addiction, or because of how they intersect with other media: Minecraft through its hit movie, Fortnite through its many collaborations with music artists. And this is the key problem. Mainstream media is still at the stage where every single games story that does make it to TV or radio has to do the job of explaining and justifying the whole industry. It’s time for programme-makers to understand that video games are a mass cultural phenomenon. Enough people play them and understand them so that they don’t have to be re-introduced every time they’re covered. And most importantly, there is life, love, art and brilliance beyond Grand Theft Auto and beyond the coming storm of hype.

It was my birthday a couple of weeks ago, so I set out to find a simple, fun video game that the whole family could enjoy – and I wanted to share my discovery.

Inspired by Dominik Diamond’s recent column on this very subject, I downloaded the party game What The Dub?!, in which players watch old film clips with portions of the sound dubbed out and then enter their own amusing dialogue to fill the gap. The clips are then re-shown with each player’s text added to the soundtrack via a stilted robotic voice – then everyone votes on the funniest entry. It was hilarious, especially because the clips are from weird old public domain films and TV shows, so everything feels stilted and ridiculous. It’s also simple to take part, with each player using their phone to enter their dialogue choices. Apparently, it’s possible to add new clips via the Steam Workshop, the digital store’s user-generated content feature, but we didn’t figure that out. Regardless, What the Dub?! will definitely be revived at future family celebrations.

Available on: PC

 Estimated playtime: All evening!

EA staff have been speaking anonymously to the industry-news site Game Developer about their concerns after the Saudi-led buyout of Electronic Arts. Some are troubled by the prospect of popular games such as EA Sports FC, Madden and Battlefield being used by Saudi Arabia to distract from its poor human rights record. There are also worries about the company’s culture and job security.

TV producers looking for interesting game stories that don’t involve GTA could check out Eurogamer’s excellent article on the No Man’s Sky’s Galactic Hub project. It’s a community of players exploring and scientifically cataloguing specific regions of the long-running space adventure sim, like a sort of ragtag Starfleet mission. Live long and prosper, lads.

As if making and marketing independent video games isn’t hard enough, several developers have reported thefts at this year’s Gamescom event in Cologne. Posting on X, Mimic creator Ryan Laley said: “Our equipment was stolen last night from the booth. Police reports have been filed. At a loss for words to describe the feeling. Just defeated. Gonna do my best with what’s left of the week. But a huge blow financially and mentally.” According to VGC, others affected included publisher iam8bit and Tessera Studios.

A question from Richard via email:

“My son, aged 6, is a big fan of aeroplanes and is really interested in flight. What games are there that could be used to entertain him, as a thing to do with me. I have (ridiculously) a PS5 and Xbox Series X – is Flight Simulator right? How about Ace Combat? Anything else?”

I’d definitely recommend Microsoft Flight Simulator, which is available on PS5 and Xbox. It can be controlled with just a joypad and you can switch off all the technical elements for your son so he’s basically just steering the craft like in an arcade game. There are lots of aircraft to fly, from tiny prop planes to passenger jets, and you can choose anywhere on Earth to explore. I love simply zooming over cities and scenic highlights, taking it all in.

If you’re ok with him doing a bit of shooting, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is out in October, promising highly detailed visuals and exciting dogfighting. Fans say it looks to be a highlight for the series. I’d also recommend No Man’s Sky, which is a space exploration game, but the flight feels lovely, whether you’re scorching over the surface of a planet or out in the depths of the cosmos. The controls are extremely intuitive too. If he gets into space flight, the slightly more involved Elite Dangerous is worth a look, and for an accessible combination of space flight and shooting, Everspace: Stellar Edition is a really nice option on PS5.

title: The Seven Coolest Inventions From 'DEF CON' 2026
description: The world's largest hacker convention showcased these cutting-edge devices and platforms.
fullText:
DEF CON, the annual hacker convention held in Las Vegas, Nevada, just concluded its 2026 event. Between the convention’s Main Stage talks, vendor floors, and Demo Labs displays, this year’s event displayed some amazing feats of anti-surveillance technology built by open-source and independent developers or cybersecurity experts.

There’s a device that detects nearby Flock cameras, an encrypted handheld device for sending texts without relying on carrier networks or the internet, a risk calculator for third-party web browser extensions, and an advanced spyware detector for smartphones. I spent my weekend analyzing all of them, going through reams of on-the-floor footage and announcement pages. These are the things that struck me as most interesting.

Flock Safety’s automated license plate reading (ALPR) cameras have been the focus of every cybersecurity and surveillance conversation in 2026. They quietly scan license plates to send out automatic alerts to law enforcement and federal agencies, with the advertised goal of cracking down on criminal activity. However, that's not always the case: Reports show law enforcement has used Flock data to track immigrants and people potentially seeking abortions, as well as spy on partners and romantic interests.

A very interesting gadget to come out of DEF CON 2026 is this technology developed by a DIY hardware enthusiast who goes by “Colonel Panic.” It’s a lightweight firmware called Flock-You that can be installed on any ESP32 microcontroller.  You buy an ESP32 chip for $10 to $15, load the firmware onto it, and use it to listen for wireless signals that alert you when a surveillance camera like Flock is nearby. If you don’t want to bother yourself with the DIY setup, Colonel Panic also sells packaged ESP32 boards with the Flock-You firmware pre-loaded into them. These are called OUI-SPY detectors, and you can get them for as little as $85 apiece.

There are a few caveats, like how the Flock-You firmware won’t work on Arduino or Raspberry Pi microcontrollers because they are tuned into the ESP32’s specific wifi and Bluetooth infrastructure. Also, Flock cameras are already being adjusted to evade this detection technology, so it will probably only work on older or unpatched models.

If there was ever a Swiss Army knife of anti-surveillance tech, Biscuit Ultra is probably it. This is a handheld device designed by a hacker known as Hedge that scans nearby wireless signals for several telltale signs of surveillance tech in your vicinity. Then it will feed you information like:

A list of all nearby wifi networks

Flock or Axon cameras in your range

If the same device or gadget keeps popping up everywhere you go

Of the three features, I think the third one is probably the most useful of the bunch. You’ll get automated alerts if the same smartphone, tracker, or GPS device is following you around over time, which is a good indicator of whether you’re being actively tracked without your knowledge. The device is designed to look inconspicuous, like a small handheld router with two swivel antennas. Right now, a single unit costs about $160 on the Biscuit Shop.

Law enforcement officials in the United States use devices called IMSI-catchers (nicknamed “Stingrays”) that can track cellphones by pretending to be a cell tower. They send out strong signals that phones mistake for a real tower, which leads them to disconnect from the local tower and connect to the catcher instead. Once connected, Stingrays can track your real-time location and call logs without anyone the wiser. It’s a technique commonly used by local police departments, the FBI, and ICE, for example. Worse still, when these devices are active, they catch stray data from all other cellphones in the vicinity, even if their owners weren’t persons of interest in an investigation.

Federal agents are required to obtain a search warrant before deploying these tools except in "exigent circumstances," but that likely isn't enough to preserve the general public's privacy. The Electronic Frontier Foundation has developed a new tool called Rayhunter to detect any suspicious towers that could be Stingrays in the vicinity. It runs on any off-the-shelf mobile hotspot, which the EFF says can cost as little as $20. You simply load the EFF’s free software into the hotspot, and it lights up red if there’s any suspicious tracking behavior from nearby towers.

Exploitee.rs is a cybersecurity research group that specializes in IoT security, home automation, entertainment devices, and smartphones. They built a radio communication device called The Hacker Pager, which looks like a retro-style handheld smartphone with a screen and mechanical keyboard.

Unlike cellphones, The Hacker Pager does not rely on cell towers or internet connectivity. This low-tech gadget uses radio waves that transmit from device to device instead, based on an open-source firmware called Meshtastic. With the 2026 firmware update, Exploitee.rs’ device now supports external Bluetooth keyboards, multichannel communication, and more customization options for things like notification sounds. While secure, it’s not very long-distance, because the signals only travel up to thirty miles—assuming that there's a clear line of sight with no obstructions.

This one’s still a prototype, but it’s worth a look anyway for the idea alone. Makoto Sugita, or “Mr. Rabbit,” showed off a deniable storage system that can create a fake version of your local file storage. That way, you can keep confidential data hidden from the people around you.

Phasmid is an open-source Python app that can be installed on a device that splits your local storage into two slots—one real, and the other a fake version that you designed with your sensitive data removed. When someone tries to physically coerce you into handing over your device, Phasmid pulls up a “safe” version of your local storage that has all the sensitive data scrubbed from it, without revealing anything else.

Since it’s only a prototype, Phasmid can only be installed on Raspberry Pi devices for now, and a macOS version is currently under development. It’s more of a proof of concept as it stands, but an interesting look at a tool that solves a specific problem that not a lot of technology is designed to secure against.

Fake extensions with security issues have been a recurring concern for web browsers. Many of these extensions also pretend to be ad blockers or coupon finders, quietly tracking your online activity, logging keystrokes, or switching on your mic and webcam. Most people don’t even notice such a thing until they receive a ransom email or end up in a data breach. L.A.Y.E.R.S., designed by cybersecurity researchers Abhinav Khanna and Krishna Chaganti, scans your currently installed browser extensions to assign each a risk score based on their behavior patterns.

L.A.Y.E.R.S. is currently available as a downloadable package on GitHub. It runs locally on your web browser, without sending any data to third-party platforms via API. Every browser extension you have installed gets scanned for suspicious permission requests, malicious JavaScript or HTML, risky external endpoint URLs, and other common patterns among malicious plugins. You end up with a simple risk score that grades each extension between one and 100, with lower scores indicating a higher security risk.

IsMyPhonePwned offers an answer to the question: “What should I do if I think my phone has spyware on it?” Normally, you’d be forced to employ expensive forensic cybersecurity experts or pay for an antimalware platform like BitDefender or Norton. But Anthony Desnos developed IsMyPhonePwned as a free alternative to expensive spyware detectors that require you to install a cumbersome app on your phone which would also give away your suspicions to the attacker.

Desnos’ tool is a web application you can run from your desktop PC. You connect to your compromised smartphone over USB, and IsMyPhonePwned generates a bug report for you. You can run this check on both Android and iOS devices. If you suspect a specific app of being spyware, there’s also a tool here called droid2web that can scan Android app packages separately.

title: Sri Lanka stripped of hosting Women's Champions Trophy
description: The International Cricket Council moves the inaugural edition of next year's Women's Champions Trophy from Sri Lanka to India.
fullText:
Next year's inaugural Women's Champions Trophy has been moved from Sri Lanka to India by the International Cricket Council.

Sri Lanka had been due to stage the six-team event but have been stripped of the hosting rights because of ongoing issues with its national board and government interference.

A statement from the ICC said Sri Lanka Cricket is continuing "to make the requisite reforms" which were outlined at the global governing body's annual conference in July.

Bangladesh and South Africa were also interested in staging the tournament but the ICC board ratified India as replacement hosts for the event, with matches to be held in Mumbai and Vadodara.

Unlike the men's Champions Trophy, which is a 50-over-a-side competition, the women's event will be a T20 tournament.

It will be played on a round-robin basis with the top two sides progressing to the final.

Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka are the six teams who will take part, having been the highest-ranked sides at the qualification cut-off date of 6 July.

title: Paredes puts question mark over Argentina future
description: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes says it is going to be "difficult" for him to continue playing for his country in the wake of his 10-match international ban.
fullText:
Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes says it is going to be "difficult" for him to continue playing for his country in the wake of his 10-match international ban.

Paredes received the suspension from Fifa for his part in an on-pitch confrontation following Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

The 32-year-old grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground, before appearing to strike the latter in the face.

Paredes also suggested Argentina legend Lionel Messi retiring from international football could play a part in his decision.

"It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team," said Boca Juniors player Paredes.

"Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

"I haven't discussed it with the coach [Lionel Scaloni] yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make."

Argentina's Paredes banned for 10 games

Messi retires from Argentina duty with 'nothing left to give'

Messi, 39, recently announced his retirement from international football, saying he had "nothing left to give" having "given it my all".

He captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022 but could not repeat the feat against Spain in his final game for his country.

title: Are Arsenal taking a risk in not signing a world-class forward?
description: Arsenal have been busy in the transfer market as they look to defend their Premier League title, but do they lack a world class striker still?
fullText:
"Very ambitious, very fast, and very smart."

That was manager Mikel Arteta's aim for Arsenal's transfer dealings following their defeat by Paris St-Germain in the Champions League final in May.

The Gunners won their first title in 22 years last season by seven points and did not lose a game in the Champions League during normal time, with their only loss in the competition coming to Luis Enrique's side on penalties.

But it was clear coming into the summer transfer window that the club were looking for a game-changing attacker to lift their forward line.

Viktor Gyokeres - a £64m signing last summer from Portuguese side Sporting - scored 21 goals in his first season for Arsenal but his performances still raised questions about whether he is the best fit for Arteta's side going forward.

The same debate was posed on the left wing with Leandro Trossard's form dipping after starting the season well and Gabriel Martinelli, despite scoring six goals in the Champions League campaign, scoring just once in the league.

And now both of those players have left the club.

But finding an attacker who could elevate a squad that almost won a domestic and European double proved difficult.

Arsenal want to be one of the best clubs in the world.

In an interview with the Times, chief executive Richard Garlick said that joining the world's super-clubs is "the goal - that's the ambition".

In that same interview, Garlick acknowledged that the "pool of players is smaller now than it was a few years ago if we're going to improve".

And unfortunately for the Gunners, they have found that out this summer.

Sporting director Andrea Berta is known for speaking to multiple targets at once while preparing the deals simultaneously.

The Gunners went into this window with interest in Morgan Rogers, Bradley Barcola, Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr.

Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius Jr turned public and was shaped around his contract situation at Real Madrid.

Ultimately, the Spanish club offered him a bigger package than they had done before Arsenal's interest stepped up.

But inside the club, there was a period where they thought they were going to be successful in bringing one of the best wingers in world football to north London.

Questions will be posed as to why the club did not go big for Rogers, but Arsenal stuck to their valuation of £80m before Chelsea then paid £117m for the former Aston Villa forward.

That left Julian Alvarez as the only available target in the window after Liverpool succeeded in bringing in Bradley Barcola.

Arsenal always had reservations about paying the fee needed to get Barcola too.

It appeared Alvarez's only way out of Atletico Madrid was Arsenal, after Atleti were adamant that they would not negotiate with Barcelona.

However, Alvarez returned to training with the Spanish side and, despite Arteta's best efforts laying out plans to the player, the deal did not come off.

Arteta joins elite 250 club - but where does he rank?

Arsenal's Nwaneri joins Dortmund on loan

Arsenal showed the strength of their squad in their win over Aston Villa on Monday night.

They brought in Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes for £75m, Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa (£55m), turned Piero Hincapie's loan deal into a permanent one (£34.5m) and signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m.

Tzolis struggled in the win but has already impressed in the Community Shield victory over Manchester City and the opening day Premier League win over Coventry.

Guimaraes is being described by some as one of the signings of the window, and Konsa was statistically the best defender in the league for ground duel success (73.1%) and passing accuracy (95%) last season.

Konsa, although he brings the number of senior defenders in Arsenal's squad to eight, was brought in because of the injuries to William Saliba and Jurrien Timber.

A big part of Arsenal's window has been who they have let go too.

Gabriel Martinelli is close to completing a move for around £60m to Al-Hilal, which would be a record sale for the club.

Leandro Trossard has moved to Besiktas (£15.3m), while Christian Norgaard was sold to Everton (£7m).

The main worry from supporters is that they have let two forwards go who play on the left wing and brought in just one to replace them.

There is no denying that Arsenal wanted a game-changing attacker this summer - if there was one available.

Not signing one this window does leave them with the chance to act again in January or wait completely until next summer to try to bring in a new forward.

But there will be uncomfortable conversations about why there hasn't been one during this window, even if the football leadership team are content with the business the club has done.

Questions will of course be asked of Arteta, Berta and co-chair Josh Kroenke as to why, after Arsenal's success, such an attractive club weren't able to get one of their targets over the line.

However, there is no denying that Arsenal's squad is one of the best in Europe. Their bench for the win over Aston Villa contained nine full internationals with two of those - Merino and Zubimendi - World Cup winners.

Gabriel Jesus has moved to Barcelona for £12.8m, and although he was not an integral part of Arsenal's team because of selection and fitness issues, he still made 27 appearances in all competitions, scoring six goals.

With Martinelli and Trossard both gone, there will be more opportunity for Eberechi Eze to play from the left wing, a position he shone in at former club Crystal Palace.

Eze played in some of the biggest games of Arsenal's last campaign on the left wing and put in an impressive appearance in that role in the win over Villa on Monday too.

Last season, Kai Havertz missed large parts of the campaign with injury, while Mikel Merino, another option to play at striker, missed a chunk of the season too but both have started this season fully fit.

Those injuries last season meant that Gyokeres had to lead the line for long periods without back-up in his first campaign with Arsenal, but despite that test, it does not take away that the Swedish international's suitability is still in question.

It is also intriguing that Gyokeres has not played a minute of the opening two Premier League matches so far.

Arsenal are still looking like the early season favourites and have the potential to defend their title, but criticism surrounding the lack of a new forward will be tough to avoid if goals start to become hard to come by.

title: Rybakina makes winning start in race to number one
description: Elena Rybakina says she is "motivated" by the race to become world number one but is simply taking things "day by day" after getting her US Open campaign off to a winning start.
fullText:
Elena Rybakina says she is "motivated" by the race to become world number one but is simply taking things "day by day" after getting her US Open campaign off to a winning start.

Playing for the first time since withdrawing midway through her Cincinnati Masters quarter-final with a heel injury last month, Rybakina showed no signs of discomfort as she eased to a dominant 6-3 6-2 win over 17-year-old wildcard Thea Frodin.

The 27-year-old second seed trails Aryna Sabalenka by just 434 points in the world rankings and will become number one for the first time by reaching the semi-finals in New York – even if Sabalenka defends her title.

Regardless of her performance, Rybakina will also secure the top ranking if none of Sabalenka, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula lift the trophy.

"I'm definitely motivated [to become world number one]," said Rybakina, who trailed Sabalenka by more than 3,000 points in the spring before the Belarusian entered a mid-season slump.

"I feel like I had opportunities before and it didn't go my way. It will be an amazing achievement but it's still too far and I need to focus on my day off tomorrow, my recovery, and just keep on going."

Fighting to stay No 1 - Sabalenka's US Open mission

Sabalenka wins to begin bid for US Open 'three-peat'

Rybakina, a two-time Grand Slam winner, arrived at Flushing Meadows with question marks around her fitness after retiring injured against Iga Swiatek in Cincinnati.

Though she looked comfortable on court, her movement went largely untested by Frodin - who acted as Serena Williams' body double in the Oscar-nominated film 'King Richard' - as she blew the world number 585 away on serve and dictated points from the baseline.

"We didn't know if [I was] going to be able to play here or not. I'm pretty happy that I'm playing right now, and we are taking [it] day by day," Rybakina said about her injury.

"I was not playing for the full week [before the tournament], so seven days no tennis and basically not too much gym I could do movement-wise.

"So it's a great result after 10 days from that kind of injury."

After opening the rain-delayed match with a double fault, Rybakina proved relentless on serve, dropping just three points and reeling off three consecutive love holds in the first set.

She didn't face a break point until the sixth game of the second set, saving both.

Equally clinical in Frodin's service games, she converted her first three break points to race into a set and 5-1 lead.

However, the young wildcard, making her WTA Tour main-draw debut after winning the United States Tennis Association (USTA) Girls' 18s National Championship, made Rybakina work to get over the line, saving three match points with aces in her final service game among 11 across the match.

Rybakina served out the win with an ace of her own – her sixth of the match and a tour-leading 363rd of the season.

"She played really well today. She has great shots, great serve, it was no easy," Rybakina said of the largely unknown Frodin.

Serena Williams is set for a rematch with Maya Joint, who beat the American great in three sets on her singles return at Wimbledon in June, in the women's doubles.

Williams, partnering her sister Venus at a Grand Slam for the first time since 2022, has been drawn against Australian Joint and Chan Hao-chingof Taiwan.

The Williams sisters, who were awarded a wildcard to compete in New York, won 14 double titles together between 1999 and 2016, including two US Opens.

They were due to renew their partnership at Wimbledon but Serena picked up a knee injury in her 6-3 6-7 (6-8) 6-3 first-round defeat by Joint.

title: What awaits USWNT during 2027 Women’s World Cup qualification
description: The USWNT doesn’t need to do much to qualify, but they should not take it for granted.
fullText:
The 2027 Women's World Cup is less than 11 months away as 32 teams will gather in Brazil for the tournament. For the United States women's national team, it's a chance to try and get back to being world champions after their title was snatched in 2023 after holding it for eight years.

Now that the Women's World Cup match schedule has been released, all attention is starting to shift towards qualification. But, what does the USWNT need to do to qualify for the Women's World Cup?

We take a look at the road to the 2027 Women's World Cup and what awaits the USWNT this fall.

The October international window is the final round of friendlies before the qualification tournament. The USWNT, ranked second in the FIFA world rankings, plays a pair of friendlies against Spain, the top ranked team and defending Women's World Cup champions. It's not only a huge pair of matches between the top two ranked teams in the world, but also a barometer test.

Then, the November-December international window is when the 2026 Concacaf W Championship will take place in Texas. The tournament serves as both Women's World Cup qualifying and qualification for the 2028 Olympics. Eight teams (USA, Canada, Mexico, Jamaica, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Haiti, and Panama) will compete in a single elimination tournament over the course of nine days in Mansfield, TX and Houston.

The quarterfinal round is the most important for the USWNT in terms of World Cup qualifying. Should they win their quarterfinal match against El Salvador on Nov. 27, the opening match of the tournament, they will qualify directly for the 2027 Women's World Cup. The four quarterfinal winners earn Concacaf's direct bids to the tournament in Brazil.

Should the unexpected happen and the USWNT loses to El Salvador, they would still have a chance to qualify via a series of playoffs. The four quarterfinal losers will move to the play-in round, as Concacaf has two slots in the FIFA Women's World Cup playoffs in February. To fill those slots, the four quarterfinal losers will play, with the winners moving onto the FIFA playoff. For the USWNT, should they be in the play-in round, they would face the loser of the Jamaica-Costa Rica quarterfinal.

The rest of the 2026 Concacaf W Championship, in addition to crowning the region's champion, will be used for Olympic qualifying. Since the 2028 Olympics will be hosted in Los Angeles, the USWNT has an automatic spot as hosts. The top three teams not named the United States at the Concacaf W Championship will also book their place in the 2028 Olympics.

For the USWNT, winning one match to directly qualify for the Women's World Cup may seem like an easy thing, but the players cannot take it for granted. The team doesn't have to look back that far to see what happens when there's a slip-up in the qualification. In 2010, after losing to Mexico in the semifinals of the Concacaf W Championship, the USWNT needed a FIFA playoff win over Italy to qualify for the 2011 Women's World Cup.

Head coach Emma Hayes wants to leave no doubt and qualify directly this time around so attention can turn towards World Cup preparation. After the October friendlies against Spain are complete, the USWNT will focus on winning the Concacaf W Championship and booking tickets to Brazil in the process.

title: Germany legend Antonio Rüdiger announces international retirement with touching message

fullText:
After appearing in three FIFA World Cups and two UEFA European Championships for Germany, legendary defender Antonio Rüdiger has announced his decision to step down from international duty.

The 33-year-old Real Madrid star, who appeared in all four of Germany's World Cup games this summer in North America, where they were knocked out in the Round of 32 by Paraguay on penalties, has been a regular for his country when fit for much of the past 12 years.

But now, with Jürgen Klopp having recently taken over from Julian Nagelsmann as the national team's head coach, it seems Rüdiger believes it's time for him to clear the way for the next wave of talent.

"After some time spent reflecting, the moment has come for me to end my career with the national team and clear the way for the young generation," he wrote on social media, via an online translation.

"When I first wore the DFB jersey in 2014, I never could have imagined in my wildest dreams that it would ultimately lead to 86 international matches.

"Even though the big title eluded us at the last tournaments and we had to endure some painful defeats, this time was an incredibly special chapter for me—one that will shape me forever.

"A huge thank you goes to: My teammates: For every shared duel and the camaraderie in the locker room and at the team hotel—and above all, for the friendships that will endure far beyond football.

"The entire coaching and support staff: Thank you for the years of trust and the work behind the scenes. Rüdiger retires having scored three goals and provided five assists during his tenure with the national team, with whom he won the Confederations Cup in 2017 and reached the EURO 2024 quarter-finals.

He can now focus solely on his club career with Madrid, which he has called home since leaving Chelsea after five seasons back in 2022. A two-time Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup, and Copa del Rey champion - amongst numerous other accolades with both the Blues and Los Blancos - Rüdiger was an unused substitute for Madrid's first two La Liga games this season, but played the full 90 in their recent 4-0 win against Málaga CF.

title: ‘Should Never Play for Team US Again’ – WNBA World Reacts As USA Head Coach Shrugs Off A’ja Wilson Absence Question

Although the likes of Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, and Angel Reese will be playing for Team USA, it came as a surprise to many that Team USA will be without Las Vegas Aces' star A'Ja Wilson.

Wilson, the number one overall pick of the 2018 draft, is having another outstanding season, averaging 26.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.0 blocks, and 1.4 steals in 32.0 minutes per game.

Wilson is shooting 52.3% from the field and 39.8% from three. Wilson is a three-time WNBA champion, two-time Finals MVP, eight-time All-Star, three-time Defensive Player of the Year, and four-time MVP.

Simply put, she is one of, if not the, best player in the WNBA right now, so it's clear why her absence has drawn so many questions.

Another mainstay, Kelsey Plum of the Phoenix Mercury, also won't be playing due to injury. Team USA head coach Kara Lawson gave her reaction to the news.

"Both of them [Kelsey Plum included] obviously have been great players for us, and I'll miss being around them, but ultimately, we've kind of moved on…" Lawson said. "We don't have time to be worried about who's not here. We've got to really focus on ourselves."

That's the only kind of mindset that Lawson can have at this time. Of course, with an incredible roster still miles more talented and deeper than any other country, it's probably easy to get over a couple of key players missing the tournament.

Lawson addressed several issues but said she had not spoken with A'ja Wilson about her decision not to play in the World Cup. Sue Bird apparently handled that.

"I didn't have any conversation with A'ja (Wilson)," Lawson said.

Wilson certainly isn't required to play in the tournament, but not having a conversation with Lawson prior to the decision becoming public is definitely going to strike some the wrong way. The CDS Sports Podcast weighed in and had nothing kind to say about Wilson's decision.

Obviously, they may have gone a little far, but you can see the anger is there. Coach Anderson thinks Lawson is upset with Wilson's choice.

They wrote: "Damn! Kara Lawson seems upset about A'ja Wilson quitting on her team so late!"

Whether it's quitting on the team is debatable, but you can see why Lawson may be upset. Leena points out that no one really knows why Wilson isn't playing.

"So is Aja sick or injured? I'm so confused on how nobody from Team USA knows what's going on with her?"they asked. It's an interesting question, and the uncertainty will only lead to more questions and speculation.

Shraddha thinks Wilson should have been more 'professional.' "That sounds bad," they said. "A'ja was not professional about it at all."

All in all, this does not seem like it was handled well on Wilson's part, and that's only going to add fuel to the fan's fire.

title: Official | Borna Sosa returns to the Bundesliga via Cologne loan
description: Cologne have officially completed the signing of Croatian international Borna Sosa from Crystal Palace. The 28-year-old left-back joins the cathedral city side on loan through the end of the 2026/27 c...
fullText:
Cologne have officially completed the signing of Croatian international Borna Sosa from Crystal Palace. The 28-year-old left-back joins the cathedral city side on loan through the end of the 2026/27 campaign. No purchase option is reportedly included in the agreement. The deal concludes a deadline-day pursuit that accelerated considerably over the past 48 hours.

The defender reached a verbal agreement with Köln before the two clubs completed the remaining negotiations ahead of the deadline. Sosa joins fellow 28-year-old Gideon Mensah as another natural option on the left side and provides Cologne with considerable Bundesliga experience.

The Bundesliga remains the competition most closely associated with the strongest period of Sosa's club career. Sosa played for Stuttgart for five seasons between 2018 and 2023. At one point near the end of the 2020/21 Bundesliga campaign, Sosa even emerged as a potential German national team option after obtaining German citizenship.

Stuttgart signed the Zagreb native from Dinamo Zagreb in 2018. Following relegation during his first season, Sosa helped the Swabians immediately return to the top flight and subsequently established himself as one of the Bundesliga's most productive attacking wing-backs.

His exceptional left foot became his defining feature. Sosa supplied 35 assists and scored five goals across 115 competitive appearances for Stuttgart, repeatedly creating chances with early deliveries and crosses from advanced positions on the left.

His performances also earned him regular international recognition with Croatia and helped establish a market value that peaked at €23m. Sosa eventually left Stuttgart for Ajax in September 2023 in a deal worth approximately €8m.

What followed proved considerably less successful. The Croatian spent only one season in Amsterdam before moving to Torino on loan for the 2024/25 campaign. The Serie A side declined to exercise its purchase option, leaving Sosa to return briefly to Ajax before Crystal Palace acquired him for approximately €2.3m last summer.

Regular football again proved difficult to secure in England.

Cologne have finally supplied the route back.

Sosa's arrival gives Kwasniok a stylistically different option to Mensah. The former Stuttgart wing-back remains most comfortable when permitted to advance aggressively down the left, and his crossing quality gives Cologne another means of creating chances from wide areas. The transfer also brings considerably more experience to a Cologne squad seeking to consolidate its Bundesliga status after last season's 14th-place finish.

Sosa arrives having played Bundesliga, Eredivisie, Serie A, Premier League and European football, while also representing Croatia extensively at international level.

His first possible Bundesliga appearance back in Germany carries an additional twist.

Cologne travel to Stuttgart on Matchday 2.

"We are very pleased that Borna will strengthen us this season," Kessler said in Cologne's club statement. "He knows the Bundesliga very well from his time with VfB Stuttgart and possesses valuable international experience."

"At the same time, through our conversations we got to know him as a very reflective and positive person whose personality fits us very well and who will also contribute his experience off the pitch," Kessler continued. "With his strong left foot, his attacking drive and his high quality when crossing, he expands our possibilities and gives our game additional options."

"I know Cologne from my time in Stuttgart," Sosa himself added. "I still remember the away games very well because Cologne has one of the best atmospheres in the Bundesliga. Now I'm looking forward to experiencing that feeling as an FC player and playing here in the stadium. I've obviously followed how FC have started because I still follow the Bundesliga."

title: Surprise: Liverpool pick striker to backup Alexander Isak
description: Alexander Isak will be expected to finally get his Liverpool career off the ground this season.The Sweden international spent the vast majority of the 2026-27 campaign on the bench which is far from i...
fullText:
Alexander Isak will be expected to finally get his Liverpool career off the ground this season.

The Sweden international spent the vast majority of the 2026-27 campaign on the bench which is far from ideal for a club-record signing.

However, now that he's back fit and raring to go, Andoni Iraola will undoubtedly be looking towards the towering striker to lead his attack.

Isak has already managed to get his first Premier League goal of the season but, from the way that he's performed so far, he doesn't look like he's worth anywhere the £125 million that Liverpool spent on him.

But, with Hugo Ekitike out until at least January, Isak is going to have to step up his game or Liverpool will be forced to get creative.

Liverpool's academy is easily one of the best in the Premier League.

Legends such as Jamie Carragher, Steven Gerrard and Trent Alexander-Arnold have all made their way through the Anfield ranks and have gone on to be written in Liverpool's history books.

Indeed, some, such as Alexander-Arnold and Curtis Jones may have packed their bags and left but that doesn't mean that they're not talented.

At the moment, it feels like Liverpool have a lot of solid youngsters who are on the verge of breaking into Liverpool's first-team squad.

Lewis Koumas, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell have all been linked with having a regular role for Iraola this term.

But now, a player who fans thought would be exiting Anfield could be about to become Isak's backup.

"An update on Jayden Danns: he is going to remain at Liverpool with the aim of showing he can contribute for Andoni Iraola," Dominic King shared via X.

"It's a significant, too, as if the 134-year sequence of a local player representing the club is to continue, Danns will be the one to do it."

Liverpool's attack is one of their main areas to have had a question mark hanging over it this summer.

The transfer of Bradley Barcola was finally announced after what felt like months of negotiations and, Victor Munoz was also handed his first Premier League start for the club.

However, since some of the Reds' players are still carrying injuries from last term, some aren't available to play for Liverpool right from the start.

One of those being, Ekitike. As mentioned, the former Frankfurt man suffered a season-ending injury towards the end of last term and isn't scheduled to return until January at the earliest.

This means that, among their senior players, only Isak is a natural striker.

But, since Liverpool were undecided about what to do with Danns, they now seem to be giving him a chance to prove his worth.

Danns has had a tough time with injuries over the last couple of years but, now that he's fit and ready to play, this could be the best chance he'll ever get to prove why he deserves to be a Liverpool player.

Here's hoping he doesn't bottle it as, a homegrown striker could be exactly what the Reds need right now.

Monaco have dropped their asking price for Lamine Camara (22) to €50m plus add-ons, according to a report from Romain Molina. title: Superb England crush Ireland with record ODI chase
description: Maia Bouchier's stunning century helps England women seal their record one-day international chase of 282 to beat Ireland in the series opener.
fullText:
First ODI, Uptonsteel County Ground, Leicester

Ireland 281-5 (50 overs): Lewis 69 (89), Hunter 62 (90), Stokell 54* (48)

England 283-4 (38.1 overs): Bouchier 104 (95), Dunkley 73 (61); Murray 3-58

England won by six wickets; lead series 1-0

England's new era started with a dominant six-wicket win over Ireland as they cruised to their record chase of 282 in the first one-day international.

Opener Maia Bouchier struck a stunning 104 off 95 balls to secure England's highest chase in women's ODIs with 11.5 overs to spare.

Bouchier added 143 for the first wicket with Sophia Dunkley, who made 73, which laid the perfect platform before the centurion holed out to long-on with just 59 runs needed.

Alice Capsey and Freya Kemp made light work of those remaining runs with a quickfire stand of 54 off 38 balls to put England within touching distance, Capsey hitting the winning boundary to finish unbeaten on 41.

Ireland were poor with the ball and sloppy in the field, but nevertheless it was a brilliant start for England's transitional batting line-up, which is without the recently retired Heather Knight and Tammy Beaumont, and in the absence of injured captain Nat Sciver-Brunt.

Despite their struggles in the field, Ireland earlier impressed with the bat to post 281-5, with half-centuries for captain Gaby Lewis, Amy Hunter and Rebecca Stokell.

Lewis and Hunter added 136 for the second wicket before Stokell's counter-attacking knock of 54 not out from 48 balls provided a late boost, as England's bowlers lacked threat in the middle overs, without Lauren Bell and Sophie Ecclestone, who are being rested.

It looked a competitive total at the halfway mark, but on a flat pitch offering little assistance for the bowlers, the gulf in class and experience was stark in the second innings.

The three-match series continues at Derby on Thursday.

'It's an unknown' - Capsey takes England gloves for first time

Both Bouchier and Dunkley are familiar faces in England shirts, but neither has really nailed down a place in the ODI XI despite plenty of opportunities.

But with the retirements of Beaumont and Knight, two of England's finest, head coach Charlotte Edwards is building towards next summer's Ashes with places up for grabs in the top order.

Edwards and the batters know tougher tests will come - only Orla Prendergast in Ireland's line-up offers a similar threat to the world's best bowlers - but both Dunkley and Bouchier made their cases at the first time of asking.

Bouchier started watchfully, making just eight off her first 19 balls, before a flurry of boundaries off medium-pacer Jane Maguire in the sixth over kickstarted her knock.

England reached 72-0 in the powerplay, with Bouchier playing second fiddle to Dunkley, who was brutal against Ireland's wilting bowling attack in a 47-ball fifty - her fastest in ODIs.

Dunkley was caught and bowled off Cara Murray in the 20th over but Bouchier held her nerve. She took ownership as Jodi Grewcock, the new face in England's line-up, looked nervous for her nine before finding the perfect company from Capsey's proactive approach.

Bouchier looked disappointed when she was caught at long-on after a lapse of concentration, but Kemp and Capsey ensured her efforts were not wasted - the former whacked 36 off 22 to show the power of England's rapidly-improving depth, with five batters missing from the team that started the 50-over World Cup semi-final last year.

Though there are concerns for Ireland's bowling as the series continues, it was a promising start to the series for their batters as England's own bowling attack looked unthreatening without the class and experience of Bell and Ecclestone.

Wong struck early to dismiss Alice Tector for 11 with assistance from a fine one-handed catch from Capsey, who is deputising for Amy Jones as wicketkeeper and showed promised with the gloves. But overall Wong was too inconsistent, bowling five wides in her spell.

Stand-in skipper Charlie Dean held things together with 2-44 but it was a tough outing for young left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman, who bowled seven wicketless overs for 53 as the pitch offered little.

Ireland are heavily reliant on Lewis and all-rounder Prendergast, and when the latter fell for 19 after Lewis' knock of 69, there was a worry that their solid platform would be wasted.

But Stokell's dynamic knock appeared to take England by surprise as she struck the ball cleanly down the ground with regularity, and she even had to celebrate reaching fifty twice after the umpire mistakenly gave her runs for a boundary that had come off her pad.

She did eventually reach the milestone in a fifth-wicket stand of 84 with Leah Paul, but England's approach showed they would have needed a total beyond 300 to be challenging.

With two games to go, it feels like further records could be broken - especially if England are tasked with batting first.

Wales head coach Sean Lynn has named eight uncapped players in his 39-strong squad for this month's WXV Global Series fixtures.

Back-row forwards Alex Callender and Kate Williams are co-captains for the Tests against South Africa and USA at Cardiff Arms Park.

They are joined in the squad by wings Amy Williams and Kelsie Webster and prop Stella Orrin, who played in June's uncapped game against the Barbarians at Twickenham.

Five other Test novices are included – props Crystal James and Elan Jones, hooker Shanelle Williams, scrum half Megan Davey and centre Hanna Tudor.

Neumann joins Leicester Tigers after Quins exit

Callender will aim to win her first cap since the 2025 World Cup after missing the Six Nations through injury while fellow influential back-rower Kate Williams was also sidelined for the final three rounds of the championship.

Wales open their campaign against South Africa on Friday, 18 September (19:15 BST) and host USA on Saturday, 26 September (15:00 BST).

Lynn's side then go to Tokyo to face Japan on Friday, 23 October (16:00 BST) before moving on to Kumagaya for a second Test on Saturday, 31 October (07:00 BST).

All three opponents are ranked above Wales, who have dropped to 12th in the world after nine consecutive Test defeats.

But they did end their losing streak against the Barbarians at Twickenham in June when Lynn was given food for thought after fielding an inexperienced side.

"We have really moved the dial during the first three weeks of pre-season with the fitness and the rugby sessions demanding more from the squad," he said.

"The players have really pushed each other and to witness how that is driving standards in training is the reason why we have selected the squad size we have."

title: McMenamin joins Glens two months after Coleraine move
description: Northern Ireland international Conor McMenamin makes a shock switch from Coleraine to Glentoran, which comes just two months after he signed for the Bannsiders.
fullText:
Northern Ireland international Conor McMenamin has made a shock switch from Coleraine to Glentoran just two months after he signed for the Bannsiders.

As part of the deal, Joe Thomson will make the move to the Showgrounds from Coleraine on a two-year deal.

Winger McMenamin signed for Coleraine on 23 June in a high-profile move as he returned to the Irish Premiership after three years in the SPL with St Mirren.

The 31-year-old, who has struggled with a number of injuries over the past two seasons, did not start a game during his brief spell with Coleraine.

Billed as a key member of Ruaidhri Higgins' star-studded attack with the likes of Matthew Shevlin, Ben Doherty and Joel Cooper, McMenamin's move back to Glentoran is a shock transfer.

Speaking about the player's departure, Higgins said: "These things happen in football and I've no personal issue with Conor whatsoever.

"Initially part of the plan is that he'd move closer to the north coast which hasn't happened.

"I think when you do that commute from Downpatrick to Coleraine and back every day, I think it can have a negative impact on your body.

"I didn't think it was ideal, neither did Conor after a few good conversations, and we've decided to come to this arrangement which I think suits all parties."

It is a third spell at the Oval for McMenamin, who had a season at the east Belfast side in 2015-16 and then a stand-out two years from 2021 until 2023, which led to his move to Scotland.

He won the first of his 14 Northern Ireland caps in 2022 while still at Glentoran, and scored against San Marino the following year.

However, he has not featured under manager Michael O'Neill since a late cameo in the 5-1 defeat by Spain in June 2024.

"Everything has happened really quickly, but once I knew there was an opportunity to return to Glentoran, I was delighted to take it," said McMenamin.

He added: "I played some of the best football of my career here, earned my first Northern Ireland call-up and secured a move to Scotland. My three years with St Mirren were hugely important and I return as a better and more experienced player.

"This is not about looking back at what I achieved here before. I still have plenty that I want to accomplish."

McMenamin is Glentoran's sixth signing of the summer, following the arrivals of Zeno Ibsen Rossi, Greg Sloggett, Rhys Walsh, Lekan Sule and Ethan Schilte-Brown, with Walsh having since joined Annagh United.

Coleraine top the Irish Premiership table with three wins and a draw from four matches, while Glentoran are sixth with two wins and two defeats in a mixed start to their campaign.

title: Beckham and Mourinho pay tribute to Messi
description: Former England captain Sir David Beckham says Lionel Messi has inspired "millions of children worldwide," following the Argentine retiring from international football.
fullText:
Former England captain Sir David Beckham says Lionel Messi has inspired "millions of children worldwide" and his "legacy will live forever" following the Argentine's retirement from international football.

Beckham, co-owner of Messi's club Inter Miami, paid tribute to the 39-year-old's international career in which he scored 125 goals in 207 games.

Messi captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, saw them reach the final again in 2026 and won two Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024.

"This is the moment we get to look back on and realize how grateful we were to witness the greatness of a young kid with a dream," Beckham said on Instagram.

"Leo, you delivered the greatest gift to your country and, for that, your legacy will live forever. Congratulations on all you achieved for Argentina."

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho commented on Messi's retirement post on Instagram, saying "the next Copa America and the next World Cup won't be the same," without Messi involved.

Mourinho frequently managed against Messi in his first stint at Real Madrid between 2010 and 2013, a period in which the former Barcelona man won the Ballon d'Or in three consecutive years (2010-2012).

Former Argentina midfielder Angel di Maria, who also played alongside Messi at Paris St-Germain, described him as "the greatest of all time".

German international Jamal Musiala is close to his comeback at Bayern Munich and may even feature in Wednesday's German Cup match at third division Osnabrück, coach Vincent Kompany has said.

Musiala collapsed due to absence seizures in two pre-season friendlies and had to sit out the start to the season while his medication was adjusted.

Kompany said on Tuesday that there will be talks with Musiala and doctors before a decision whether Musiala can return on Wednesday, in Saturday's Bundesliga match at Schalke or next week in the Champions League against Bodø/Glimt.

"He's trained very well. It's a question of choosing the right moment; whether that's tomorrow, at the weekend or next week, I can't yet say," Kompany.

Kompany added that forward Serge Gnabry is also about to return from a thigh muscle injury he sustained in spring and made him miss the World Cup, but not yet for the Cup game.

Jonas Urbig will meanwhile be in goal for the title holders on Wednesday instead of Manuel Neuer as the youngster continues to get playing time as Neuer's career winds down.

"We've already put an incredible amount of trust in Jonas. He's played in many important matches, such as the cup final. These are milestones that show he can perform in big games," Kompany said.

Bayern are big favourites against Osnabrück but Kompany said they won't underestimate them.

"These matches are usually tough. That's part and parcel of the cup competition. You have to be mentally prepared for a real battle," he said.

"When we're on form, things often click. But it always depends on how quickly you can find the spaces and how dangerous they can become," he said.

The overall goal is however clear for the domestic double winners.

"Once you've been in the final, you always want to get there again. Our opponents were Stuttgart; they'd reached the final twice in a row. We want to achieve that now too," Kompany said.

fullText:
Last month, Microsoft’s gaming division told its workforce it was cutting 3,200 jobs, which some say will have big ramifications for game development – as well as taking a huge personal toll

On the morning of 6 July, an email went out from Asha Sharma, the chief executive of Xbox, to all of the division’s employees around the world. Under the headline “Resetting Xbox”, it announced the most significant restructuring in the history of Microsoft’s console business: 3,200 staff would be laid off throughout the financial year to 2027, and 1,600 of those roles would be eliminated immediately.

An hour later, at studios throughout company, the Teams meeting invites started arriving. “It was a virtual call with our studio manager,” says Anne Barrett, who was laid off from Bethesda Game Studios Austin. “All of our cameras and microphones were turned off so we weren’t able to say anything or react to anything. We were just brought in, told the news and it was like: ‘You guys are going to lose access to your Slack channel.’ So you saw a flurry of goodbye messages before everything was just shut off.”

This, it seems, was the routine, at least at studios in North America: a Teams call with a studio head, a prepared statement read, then a warning about Slack (the group messaging app widely used at game development studios). Emails, the staff were told, would be turned off a few days later. “We’re primarily a remote studio, so Slack is the main mode of conversation with our teammates,” says Morgan Goin, who worked at ZeniMax Online Studios. “All through the morning, everyone was sending their goodbyes … ‘Hey, it’s been great working with you. Here’s my contact information. I’ve loved working here. I will miss all of you.’” Then silence.

Bethesda Games Studios and Zenimax Online Studios were unionised in 2024 and both Goin and Barrett are on the bargaining committees for their respective studios, currently in talks with Microsoft. In the US, the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) act is a federal law that requires companies with 100 or more employees to give its workers 60 days’ notice before major closures or mass staff layoffs. Consequently, affected staff at US studios will be paid until 4 September. Union reps at Bethesda are undertaking a bargaining process with Microsoft to negotiate severance packages and any benefits owed, and is attempting to get at least some affected members re-employed. Rallies are taking place outside studio buildings across North America, with the Bethesda union seeking support from gamers via social media.

Staff say rumours had been circulating about a new wave of lay-offs for several weeks, and that they saw the Bloomberg article on 10 June warning of coming job cuts. “There was an impending sense of doom, and it was like, man, is it going to be us?” says Barrett. “We thought we were safe. I mean, Bethesda Games Studios is Skyrim, it’s Fallout. We have really highly anticipated stuff coming out. We thought that the work we were doing was going to keep us safe. And instead, we got brought into a meeting that was two minutes long, to end, in some cases, decades of career at the company. It was just devastating.”

“I remember, I laughed the whole day because I was in complete disbelief,” Barrett adds. “I was like, there’s no way they’re doing this. That’s how I processed it. Some of my co-workers were just devastated. I mean, breaking down. They did not understand what was going on. We had people who were just in really dark places. I think it hit me probably the next day. I felt like, wow – I just spent seven years doing all this. In college, people called me Bethesda because it was my dream to work here. And that was just … gone.”

This is what doesn’t get reported with the statistics of mass redundancies: the sheer human cost of it. “I’m very tired, my sleep schedule is all kinds of messed up, my eating has not been great,” says Goin. “I have to ask myself daily: have you had enough food and water? Have you had enough sunlight? When was the last time you took a shower? We’re doing the depression symptoms, that’s what’s happening. I feel like I’m grieving.”

Simon Préfontaine has a similar story. Previously a designer at Bethesda Game Studios Montreal, he is a single father concerned about the future without work, and without the health insurance his job came with. “It’s very stressful,” he says. “I’ve heard of other people who have been laid off for over a year and haven’t been able to find work. I know I’m not the only single parent in the Montreal studio, I know there are people that have health issues.” But as with Goin, it is about more than financial stability. “It might seem like an overstatement or a dramatisation, but I do feel like I went through the stages of grief. You work with these people for years and years and years, and then suddenly you don’t get to see them any more.”

What has been most bewildering to staff is that there seemed to be no structure to the layoffs, no clear reasoning behind who was affected. “I’m on the character art team, and we lost two people who had been there for decades,” says Alex Nguyen, a union bargainer still employed at Bethesda Games Studios Dallas. “They did everything that was asked, they were very passionate, they were great at their jobs. They worked on all this stuff that made our creatures, characters and armour feel real. Outstanding employees. It never made any sense.”

It is likely, after all that, there will be ramifications for games being produced at these studios – including content delays and project cancellations. Id Software, creator of Doom and Quake, lost 136 staff in the cuts – a majority of its workforce. One staff member affected, VFX artist Derek Best, claimed in a LinkedIn post that the developer had been relegated to “support studio size”.

Barrett makes a similar assertion about Bethesda, where the redundancies have been less severe but where key staff have been affected. “I don’t know how you create games at the quality level we were without the institutional knowledge that’s been lost. We have proprietary tech. Our titles have a very well-known visual identity. And when you lose the people who built the tech, when you lose the people who were improving it, you can’t just throw new people at that problem, right? You can’t replace an artist with someone brand new and say: ‘Now replicate what they were doing 15, 20 years ago.’ The company has said that they can do it. I disagree.”

Nobody knows what happens next. Barrett could only provide a brief statement on how the union’s talks with Microsoft are faring: “Effects bargaining continues with each side exchanging counterproposals. In their counter, the employer has not made enough substantial movement to care for the very real consequences impacted members are facing (loss of employment; loss of income; and disruption of benefits for their families). We (the union) have indicated that we are prepared to work toward an agreement but we cannot accept a proposal where the burden of compromise falls almost entirely on the employees.”

A Microsoft spokesperson provided the following statement on the bargaining process: “Effects bargaining for our union-represented ZeniMax colleagues is under way and on track, and we have offered severance terms comparable to the generous package provided to our non-union represented colleagues, including up to 39 weeks of severance, six months of company-paid Cobra [Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act], and 16 weeks of outplacement support. We are committed to reaching an agreement that supports impacted colleagues as they move forward.”

At least 1,600 more redundancies are coming at Xbox studios as the “reset” of the division continues. During that time, there will likely be mass lay-off events at other large companies in the industry. All of the staff I spoke to echoed a familiar feeling about mainstream games development – that something has gone drastically wrong and that mass redundancies point to a wider malaise. “Publishers have to be prepared for multi-year development cycles,” says Nguyen. “If that cost is too high, or those timelines are too long, then the game needs to scale back in some way. That might mean more indie and AA games and fewer blockbuster titles. What doesn’t work is investing in a long-term game product, and expecting profits on a yearly basis.”

Barrett concurs. “My view of the industry has definitely been damaged,” she says. “There’s been a loss of sight over why AAA games were so valuable to players. It wasn’t just that they were big and shiny. It was that [the studios] had the resources to invest in creativity. What I see now is the same formula over and over and over again. In any entertainment industry, if you do that enough times, people get tired of it. I would love for us as an industry to get back to actually being creative and investing in that creativity.”

title: Apollo to Repackage $9 Billion Oneok Stake Into Debt Deal
description: Apollo Global Management Inc. is looking to turn another multibillion-dollar corporate equity deal into investment-grade debt it can sell to investors.
fullText:
(Bloomberg) -- Apollo Global Management Inc. is looking to turn another multibillion-dollar corporate equity deal into investment-grade debt it can sell to investors.

Apollo's $9 billion stake in Oneok Inc. will be treated as permanent equity by the borrower, allowing the Tulsa, Oklahoma-based energy company to raise capital without adding conventional debt or pressuring its credit rating. The deal was announced Sunday.

Apollo is aiming to structure the deal so securities backed by its holding can get investment-grade ratings, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing confidential information. The capital is treated as a minority equity investment that's subordinated to the firm's existing debt. Apollo then slices that up into levels of seniority, some of which can be rated investment grade.

Such deals are partially placed with Apollo's insurer Athene and third-party insurers, as well as with other Apollo and client funds.

The move highlights a strategy that the New York-based alternative asset manager has been fine-tuning across a growing number of deals. Such transactions provide companies with capital that behaves like equity and avoids the leverage and risk of downgrades that come with raising debt. It's another example of how Apollo has become a go-to financier for large corporations.

Apollo has completed more than $100 billion of such transactions, including those with Intel Corp., Vonovia SE, Germany's largest residential landlord, Anheuser-Busch InBev, Air France-KLM and BP Plc. Apollo said its pipeline for deals, which include similar types of structures, tops $100 billion.

The Oneok deal was originated by Apollo's Capital Solutions business, which is led by executives including Jamshid Ehsani.

Apollo's lending model hinges on constant growth and a steady supply of highly rated assets to feed Athene's balance sheet. The firm now oversees more than $1 trillion.

The new deal will help Oneok buy Brazos Midstream Holdings' natural gas operations in West Texas for $4.4 billion and repay debt. Apollo's investment sits in a newly created holding company, ONEOK Holdings, that is structurally subordinate to ONEOK's existing senior debt, which is rated BBB.

title: Pogačar eyes world championships after successful collarbone surgery
description: Tadej Pogačar underwent successful surgery on his broken left collarbone after his heavy crash at the Vuelta a España, his team doctor Adrian Rotunno said on Monday. The operation went well, Rotunno said, adding that the Slovenian star would remain in hospital for a few days for postoperative monitoring.
fullText:
Tadej Pogačar underwent successful surgery on his broken left collarbone after his heavy crash at the Vuelta a España, his team doctor Adrian Rotunno said on Monday.

The operation went well, Rotunno said, adding that the Slovenian star would remain in hospital for a few days for postoperative monitoring.

Pogačar would travel home as soon as he was able to, where he would begin his recovery and rehabilitation under the supervision of the medical team, Rotunno said.

The injury leaves Pogačar facing a race against time to compete at the road world championships in late September. Team manager Mauro Gianetti had said before the operation that Pogačar could still target the world championships, but that a firm assessment would depend on the surgery.

"Of course it wouldn't be easy to recover for the world championships," Gianetti said on the Vuelta rest day Monday.

Pogačar, who has won the world title for the past two years, suffered a heavy crash during Saturday's eighth stage of the Vuelta. He suffered a collarbone and cervical fracture as well as a concussion.

A broken bone typically takes about six weeks to heal, although cyclists have returned to competition after four weeks in some cases.

Gianetti said he had been deeply concerned immediately after the crash.

"I was a bit relieved when he stood. I said to myself: 'OK, he is standing, walking, he wants to continue.' But of course, that was not possible."

Pogačar had been hoping to win the Vuelta for the first time this year. The five-time Tour de France winner had previously ridden the Spanish Grand Tour only once, finishing third in 2019 at the age of 20.

He also hopes to compete at the world championships in Montreal, with the road race scheduled for September 27, and at the Tour of Lombardy on October 10. Pogačar has won the Italian one-day race, known as the "Race of the Falling Leaves," four years in a row.
